subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options & ramp safeguards - HeliosBio
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@heliosbio.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@heliosbio.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated reservation options and ramp constraints

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising for our inference-heavy pipelines. Before we commit to any reserved capacity, Procurement asked me to get a clear set of options that map to our projected ramp. Two things we need clarified: a) what are realistic minimum-GPU guarantees versus starting cluster sizes for a phased ramp, and b) what staging/bursting safeguards you can provide if our production traffic spikes above forecast during month 1-3.

We're attaching a short usage forecast (attached) so you can align recommendations with our numbers. Can you please propose 2–3 reservation structures (starter / growth / committed) with explicit min-GPU floors, ramp timing, and any warmup/credits? Also flag any implications for pricing (discounts tied to min GPUs, early termination, etc.).

Procurement (cc'd) wants something they can hand to finance and legal — ideally a simple matrix. Happy to hop on a quick 30m call this week if helpful.

Thanks,
Samira
Director, ML Engineering
HeliosBio

Attachment: helios_usage_forecast.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@heliosbio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and ramp constraints

Hi Samira — great to see the forecast, thank you. I sketched three reservation lanes below to cover conservative -> aggressive ramping. I am attaching a short proposal PDF and a GPU profile CSV with expected throughput at different concurrency/seq lengths so you can map to your numbers.

Option A — Pilot Lane (low commitment)
- Start cluster: 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent)
- Minimum guaranteed floor: 2 GPUs
- Ramp: pilot (2 weeks) -> steady pilot usage month 1 (scale to 4) -> decision point at day 30
- Bursting: access to shared burst pool up to +50% for short windows; performance not SLA-backed
- Pricing: no long-term discount; pay-as-you-go for burst tokens

Option B — Growth Lane (recommended for predictable PLG usage)
- Start cluster: 16 GPUs
- Minimum guaranteed floor: 4 GPUs (reserved, billed)
- Ramp: month 0–1 stabilization, month 1–3 linear ramp to committed baseline (8–12 GPUs typical)
- Bursting: dedicated warm pool of 4 GPUs for rapid warmups; automatic prefix cache retained during bursts for +20% efficiency
- Pricing: 20% discount on base, additional 5% for 12+ month commit

Option C — Committed Production Lane
- Start cluster: 32 GPUs
- Minimum guaranteed floor: 8 GPUs
- Ramp: can schedule multi-stage activation (0–3 months) with reserved capacity pre-warmed before go-live
- Bursting & SLOs: guaranteed burst lanes and SLA-backed latency windows; automatic fallback to compatible smaller model variants if capacity constrained
- Pricing: 30% discount + warmup credits (one-time)

Safeguards and operational controls (applies to all lanes)
- Canary window (recommended 60–90 days) with auto-fallback policies
- Warmup credit: equivalent to N token processing credits (we'll bake amount to your forecast) to offset early warmup burn
- Min-GPU floor enforcement: we can set a 'soft floor' (billing credited for unused) or a 'hard floor' (billed regardless) — we recommend soft floor for pilots, hard floor for committed lanes

I've attached: helios_proposal_draft_v2.pdf, gpu_profile_table.csv. Ben and Karthik are on-copy for pricing and activation sequencing. If this looks reasonable, I'll produce a final doc with explicit monthly commit numbers and a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: helios_proposal_draft_v2.pdf (pdf), gpu_profile_table.csv (csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and ramp constraints

Stephanie / Karthik — adding a couple of pricing levers and an alternate minimum floor that sometimes helps procurement sign off quickly.

Notes:
- Alternate min floor: 2-GPU minimum with a month-to-month cadence for first 3 months (billed as soft floor with usage true-up). This reduces initial spend but increases tail latency risk if they rely on heavier concurrency.
- Pricing levers: 1) Flex credits (applied for warmup) that expire after 90 days, 2) stepped discount for commit ramps (0–3 months: baseline discount, after month 4 additional discount triggers)
- Canary recommendation: 14-day canary on Growth Lane with auto-escalation if error rate or token burn is >1.5x forecast.

Attachment: pricing_breakdown.xlsx (xlsx) — includes TCO scenarios for 8/16/32 GPU starts, and uplift assumptions for burst windows.

Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts
ben@redwoodinference.com

On a separate note: if Helios wants a lower financial commitment but tighter latency SLOs, we should propose a hybrid model: reserved baseline (4 GPUs) + dedicated pre-warm pool that is billed as a lower-rate, short-duration capacity. That often satisfies finance and engineering simultaneously.

From: Samira Khan <samira@heliosbio.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@heliosbio.com>, Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@cloudinfra.io>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options and ramp constraints

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying asks from our side:
1) Can you show month-by-month example numbers for the Growth Lane (16 start) that map to our attached forecast? Procurement wants the exact monthly invoices for months 1–6 under both a soft-floor and hard-floor billing model.
2) What is the exact mechanism for the warmup credits (how do they appear on invoice and when do they expire)?
3) If we accept a 4-GPU hard floor, can Redwood add a 30-day exit window in month 3 if our usage does not materially ramp? Procurement is asking for an escape hatch.

Also cc'ing our cloud partner Ravi who will want to align on networking/VPC peering for the private deployment option. Ravi — any initial constraints we should surface to Redwood?

We will upload a more detailed month-by-month forecast later today. If you can return a version that has a hard-floor and a soft-floor invoice view, we'll circulate to Finance on Friday.

Regards,
Samira

Attachment: helios_usage_forecast_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@heliosbio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options & ramp safeguards - HeliosBio

Samira — thanks, and appreciate the updated forecast when it's ready. I've produced a compact response below and attached a finalized reservation options PDF that includes explicit month-by-month sample invoices for months 1–6 under both soft and hard floor models. Key highlights: 

Final proposal summary (attached: helios_reservation_options_final.pdf)
- Growth Lane (recommended)
  - Start: 16 GPUs (A100-equivalent)
  - Minimum hard floor: 4 GPUs (billed monthly regardless of usage)
  - Canary: 90-day canary window (we'll monitor token burn, latency, error rates)
  - Ramp schedule (example mapping to your forecast): month 1: 4–6 avg GPUs; month 2: 6–10; month 3: 8–12; month 4–6: 12–16 (auto-scale rules in place)
  - Warmup credits: one-time 5,000 token-credit allocation applied in month 1 invoice; expires after 90 days
  - Exit/escape: 30-day exit window starting at month 3 for a hard-floor contract (requires 30 days' notice, unused committed units reconciled at last invoice)
  - Pricing: 20% baseline discount; additional 5% applied when average monthly usage exceeds 12 GPUs for two consecutive months

Pilot option (soft floor)
- Start: 8 GPUs, soft-min 2 GPUs with usage true-up; 14-day canary recommended; flex credits for warmup (applied as invoice credit, visible line-item)

Operational notes
- Billing visibility: invoices include three lines — reserved floor, burst usage, and credits used. Warmup credits appear as a negative line item in month 1 and are reconciled against burst usage automatically.
- Networking/VPC: Ravi — we recommend starting with dedicated VPC peering during canary and moving to private deployment once commit is signed. Karthik will follow up with deployment runbook and peering checklist.
- SLOs and fallbacks: we will publish a runbook that defines automatic model-variant fallback thresholds and who gets paged when burst pool utilization exceeds 70% for >10min.

Next steps
1) I will upload the month-by-month invoice examples and a DocuSign SOW link (below).
2) If Procurement agrees, we'll schedule a 30-minute finance + engineering call on Thursday to walk the invoice view.
3) Karthik will draft the peering runbook and finalize the VPC checklist.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/helios/HLB-2028-041
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1H-Helios-Reserve-Proposal

Let me know availability for the call — I'm open Thu 10–11am or Thu 3–4pm PT.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192
